scientific_reframe: Identify and separately model pathways that could yield measurable population-level change in selected physical phenotypes; do not forecast a universal future appearance.

evidence_summary.finding: Human endocrine systems mediate developmental plasticity during ontogeny.
evidence_summary.permitted_inference: Developmental exposures can be modeled separately from inherited evolution.
evidence_summary.prohibited_inference: A specified future trait direction follows from present-day environmental change.

evidence_summary.finding: Third-molar agenesis is common and heterogeneous across contributing studies.
evidence_summary.permitted_inference: Agenesis is an observable dental endpoint with geographic and demographic heterogeneity.
evidence_summary.prohibited_inference: Agenesis proves current adaptive evolution or can be conflated with extraction or impaction.

evidence_summary.finding: Culture can shape selection environments through gene-culture coevolution.
evidence_summary.permitted_inference: Technology and cultural exposures are candidate pathways requiring measurement.
evidence_summary.prohibited_inference: Culture produces immediate inherited genetic change.

evidence_summary.finding: Prior polygenic-height selection signals were strongly attenuated in an independent dataset and susceptible to population stratification.
evidence_summary.permitted_inference: Genetic summaries require ancestry-aware sensitivity analysis and conservative interpretation.
evidence_summary.prohibited_inference: Polygenic-score differences establish appearance differences between human populations.

rejected_claims: Humans will inevitably have a particular facial or body morphology.
Dietary softening proves heritable jaw evolution.
Wisdom teeth are disappearing globally because of a single adaptive process.
A polygenic score can predict an individual's future appearance.
